Sam — thanks for the clear template, that helped. Below is a pragmatic, production-focused sizing sketch (ballparks + tradeoffs) so procurement has something to work with. I kept the math conservative to account for KV cache peaks and concurrent warm sessions.

Quick summary (recommended):
- Conservative baseline (no extreme quantization): 12 x 80GB GPUs (H100/A800 class) in dedicated pool — supports ~50 steady concurrency with headroom for bursts to 120 using autoscale + burst pool.
- With int8 quantization (weight-only INT8 + FP16 for key activations): 6–8 x 80GB GPUs (same SKU family) — 30–40% capacity improvement; lower memory but similar compute needs.
- Aggressive 4-bit quant (GPTQ-style) + KV offload: 4–5 x 80GB GPUs + NVMe offload nodes — best cost per token but higher engineering ops and slightly higher latency variance.

Why (high level):
- Model weights: Lumen-70B FP16 ~140GB resident (replicated/sharded topology). Quantize to 8-bit reduces to ~35–45GB equivalent per replica (depending on scheme); 4-bit can push to ~18–25GB but requires special kernels and careful eval.
- KV cache: 32k context is the dominant driver. Typical KV (per active sequence) scales roughly linearly with context length and number of layers; for Lumen-70B we estimate ~0.9–1.4 GB of KV per active 32k session depending on layer state packing and recompute strategy.
- Concurrency math (ballpark): assume average active session holds half the max context (~16k tokens). If we target 50 concurrent steady sessions: 50 * 1.1 GB ≈ 55 GB KV resident across the cluster, but because requests are distributed we dimension per-GPU KV headroom differently (we plan for per-GPU peak of ~40–48 GB to allow hot sessions to be pinned).
- Memory layout: weights + KV + activations + runtime overhead -> totals drive the required 80GB-class GPUs or multi-GPU sharding.

Operational recommendations:
1) Start with 8 x 80GB nodes with a 4-node burst pool and reserve capacity contract for 6 months; this allows you to validate traffic patterns and refine quantization safely.
2) Enable prefix caching for the 25% reused prompts — this typically cuts token compute by ~20–30% at the cost of modest memory for cached KV snapshots.
3) Canary with 4-bit quant for non-critical routes (8k variant first) and measure quality regressions. Keep FP16/int8 for main 32k variant until evals pass.
4) Use Redwood's dynamic KV eviction to keep latency SLOs stable under bursty load.

Estimated cost direction (very rough):
- Baseline (12x80GB reserved): ~USD 115k–140k/month (includes reserved GPU+infra amortized).
- Int8 path (6–8x80GB reserved): ~USD 65k–95k/month.
- 4-bit + offload (4–5x80GB + NVMe nodes): ~USD 45k–70k/month, ops premium + potential eval cost.

Next steps I recommend:
- We run a short footprint validation (3–5 days) where we:
  * Load the model to an 80GB node with FP16 and measure exact KV bytes for your representative prompts,
  * Run an int8 conversion pass and run quality/regression checks against your key eval set,
  * Measure p95 latency and tail behavior at 40–120 QPS.

If you like, we can schedule the validation next week. I attached a short PDF with the simplified calc table (redwood-dedicated-sizing-v1.pdf) and put a draft cost table in the shared spreadsheet link.

—Nikhil

Sam — following up with a recommended operational plan and next steps if EpiGen wants to proceed to procurement.

Recommended plan (phase gated):
Phase 0 — Validation (3–5 days):
- Redwood runs footprint validation on a single 80GB node (FP16) to measure exact KV bytes for your representative 10 prompts.
- We run int8 conversion and compute quality delta on your eval set.
Deliverable: exact per-session KV bytes, validated int8 quality delta, p95 latency numbers.

Phase 1 — Canary (2 weeks):
- Provision 4 x 80GB nodes (canary pool) + 2 x 80GB burst nodes.
- Deploy FP16 primary + int8 variant on separate routes; enable prefix caching for identified reuse patterns.
- Monitor per-route cost and quality; rollback to FP16 if regression > agreed threshold.
Deliverable: production-ready config and recommended committed capacity.

Phase 2 — Reserved commit / Dedicated pool (initial):
- Recommended starting commit: 6 x 80GB reserved, with 4-node burst pool (convert to 12x if telemetry warrants).
- Term: 6 months with a 30-day opt-in for conversion to baseline FP16 pool.

Ballpark pricing and timeline:
- Validation start date: as early as 29 Jun 2027 (pending NDA/instrumentation signoff).
- Internal estimate: int8 path reduces the committed GPU count by ~35% vs baseline; final pricing will be confirmed post-validation.

Next steps for procurement:
1) Please sign the short SOW (DocuSign link above) to authorize the validation run.
2) Share the three representative prompts and the eval metric (F1/ROUGE or other) you want preserved.
3) If SOC2 evidence is required we will pull the SOC2 artifact pack (Laura, can you confirm delivery SLA).
